title: S1 (analysis_spec_SPK.md): unit inclusion criteria rework -- full-corpus result
notes: SUPERSEDES the prior back-and-forth notes on this same node (incident, misattributed reproducibility bug, two disagreeing runs) -- kept below as history, but the canonical result as of this rewrite is the FINAL run described first.

FINAL RUN (git_sha cef12b9, completed 2026-08-17T19:46:07Z, 22/22 sessions, 0 failures, ~46 min): outputs/classification/unit_inclusion_v1.csv, 9061 units (Cajal/C31o, Ivan/V182o, Joule/V198o), quality_tier {mua:4257, unstable:4026, stable:778}. New criterion (fires more during omission than during a duration-matched, non-overlapping immediately-pre-omission window; fixation firing not part of the comparison at any amplitude, per Hamm's 2026-08-17 correction): 319/9061 (3.5%) pass is_omission_inclusion_new. Old template-correlation criterion (grand_s_and_o_units.csv, fx=0 in its O+ template -- the buggy mechanism): 68/9061 (0.75%). transition_totals vs old: {gained: 288, lost: 37, unchanged_included: 31, unchanged_excluded: 8705} -- verified to sum to 9061 and to match exactly between the raw CSV and the independently regenerated stats.json.

Design, final: jnwb/unit_inclusion.py::classify_unit_omission_inclusion pools all omission_events() per unit into one paired fire-probability test against local_pre_omission_window(win) -- a window duration-matched to the omission window's own length (531ms for p2/p3/p4 slots), ending 50ms (OM_BASE_GAP_MS) before the omission window starts, so it never overlaps it. This design supersedes both the spec's original literal wording ('random event from the trial timeline') and this project's own first-cut 200ms fixed baseline -- both superseded by two direct Hamm decisions, in order: (1) 2026-08-17, 'we gotta accept unit as omission if it fires more than immediately pre omission, firing at fixation is fine; and should not collide' -- replaced the random-epoch-draw null with the immediately-pre-omission window and made non-overlap an explicit requirement; (2) same day, after a window-length confound was found (200ms baseline vs 531ms omission window mechanically inflated inclusion to 73.7%, length-artifact alone correlating r=0.60 with the observed effect) -- Hamm chose 'Duration-match to 531ms' over the shorter fixed window.

Reconciliation resolved with Hamm (2026-08-16/17): subject aliases Ivan=V182o, Cajal=C31o, Joule=V198o, all three in scope; area naming uses figstyle.AREA_ORDER as-is; min_baseline_for_s_minus_hz dropped as a hard S- gate, kept as a diagnostic column only (new wrapper in unit_inclusion.py -- unit_classification.py itself untouched, Conservation).

8 tests in tests/test_unit_inclusion.py, all passing, including the spec's own required ground-truth case: a unit firing strongly at BOTH fixation (3x-dominant, to actually trigger the old classifier's rejection -- see test docstring for why equal fx/omission rates do not) and every omission slot is retained by the new criterion and rejected by the old template-correlation mechanism (r<=0.3 threshold).

quality_tier uses stable_criterion_version=presence_ks_snr_v2 (presence>0.98 AND KS quality==1 AND snr>0.5) -- confirmed SNR is available corpus-wide on the raw NWB units table (100% non-null, spot-checked one session per subject), not gated behind the 30%-coverage unit_layers.csv. Still short of the spec's full stable definition (missing FR<100Hz-at-any-1s peak-rate check -- no existing primitive in this repo, explicitly deferred, recorded in the run's own manifest.json as stable_criterion_gap).

RNG reproducibility: fixed 2026-08-17. scripts/classify_units_omission_inclusion_v1.py derives each unit's shuffle-test seed from sha256(session_prefix:unit_row:base_seed)[:4 bytes] (_unit_seed helper), not from sequential loop-draw order off a root RNG. VERIFIED twice: (1) two same-code, same-seed reruns of a 1-session smoke test (357 units) diffed byte-identical across session/unit_row/is_omission_inclusion_new/is_s_plus/is_s_minus/risk_difference/p_value_fire_shuffle -- 0/357 rows differing, max abs risk_difference diff 0.0; (2) the FINAL full-corpus run's own stats.json, independently regenerated from its raw CSV, matches the CSV's own transition totals exactly.

HISTORY (superseded, kept for the record per Conservation -- do not re-read as current): three prior full-corpus runs exist in git/backup history before this final one. RUN #1 (245/32/36/8748 transition totals) and RUN #2/RESTORE (280/37/31/8713) disagreed with each other at nominally the same seed -- this was the loop-order RNG bug above, root-caused and fixed. A separate real incident: this session's own reproducibility-check invocation (--max-sessions 1, run twice) accidentally overwrote the canonical CSV down to a 1-session file; recovered from a pre-test backup with no data loss, restored file's stats independently re-verified against the pre-incident numbers (exact match). One further correction folded in here: an earlier version of this note misattributed a 'RUN #1 vs RUN #2, same seed, same code' framing to the loop-order bug -- on inspection that specific comparison was actually between two different NULL-WINDOW DESIGNS (an early random-epoch-draw null vs the duration-matched local-pre-omission-window design), not a same-code reproducibility failure; the loop-order bug was real and separately confirmed via the byte-identical smoke-test rerun above, independent of that misattribution.

jnwb/unit_inclusion.py::sample_null_epoch_windows (the early random-epoch-draw null primitive) is dead code -- built and unit-tested in isolation, never wired into the live classify_unit_omission_inclusion path, which uses local_pre_omission_window instead per the Hamm correction above. Left in place, unused, rather than deleted (Conservation) -- a future reader should not assume it is live.
issues: stable_criterion_version=presence_ks_snr_v2 is still short of the spec's full stable definition (missing FR<100Hz-at-any-1s peak-rate check) -- deferred, no existing primitive in this repo, recorded explicitly in the run's own manifest.json.

The old-criterion comparison in this pipeline covers only the template-correlation O+ pathway (grand_s_and_o_units.csv) per the approved plan's Decision D1 -- jnwb.unit_classification's own local-baseline O+ (31/9061, not the buggy mechanism) is carried through unmodified in the same table but is not part of the gained/lost/unchanged accounting.

No corpus-level (multi-session) automated regression test exists yet for the identity-derived-seed reproducibility property -- verification above was a manual smoke-test diff, not a committed test. tests/test_unit_inclusion.py's existing determinism test covers only a single synthetic unit and would not by itself have caught the loop-order class of bug.
